land.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

successors.note: 'Lombok and Karangasem became part of the Dutch East Indies, and were administered from Bali'; the Lombok page says the island 'was annexed to the Netherlands East Indies in 1895'.

capitals.name: Mataram (Cakranegara)
capitals.note: 'with their base in Mataram'; the Cakranegara court. The page names no earlier seat; coordinates approximate.

correction.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row: Cliopatria's Bali row stays on Bali, 25 cells in 1700 and 14 from 1849). The Lombok page: 'The Balinese had managed to take over the whole island by 1750'; the Dutch-intervention page says the Cakranegara court 'was able to rule the whole island from around 1839' and that Mataram brought its rivals under control in 1838. Neither gives an area; the shape is the island.

region.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

ledger.note: By 1750: the Balinese hold all of Lombok. 'The Balinese had managed to take over the whole island by 1750' (they had taken western Lombok 'in the early seventeenth century'); the Cakranegara court was 'a branch of eastern Bali's Karangasem Kingdom'. The Intervention page puts rule of the whole island 'from around 1839', so 1750 is the Lombok page's 'by'.

region.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

ledger.note: 1838: the Mataram kingdom masters its Balinese rivals. 'Balinese infighting resulted in the island being split into four feuding Balinese kingdoms'; 'In 1838, the Mataram kingdom brought its rivals under control.'

region.text: Karangasem on eastern Bali (placed by the researcher)

ledger.note: 1849: Karangasem on Bali under the Lombok court. After supporting the Dutch in 1849 the Cakranegara court 'was rewarded with the overlordship over Karangasem'. The page does not name the Balinese land; eastern Bali is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Mataram and Cakranegara in western Lombok, where the Dutch fought in 1894

ledger.note: 25 August 1894: the Dutch camp is attacked. The Dutch landed at Ampenan on 3 June 1894 and issued ultimatums; 'On the night of August 25, the Cakranegara force attacked the 900-strong Dutch military camp'; by the end of September 'Dutch forces have destroyed the Mataram palace'. The infobox dates the intervention 'July-November 1894'.

region.text: Karangasem on eastern Bali (placed by the researcher)

ledger.note: November 1894: Karangasem passes with Lombok. The infobox territorial change reads 'Dutch control of Lombok and Karangasem'; the overlordship over Karangasem ends with the Raja's surrender.

region.text: Mataram and Cakranegara in western Lombok, where the Dutch fought in 1894

ledger.note: 20 November 1894: the Raja surrenders. 'On 8 November 1894, the Dutch made systematic artillery bombardments on the palace'; 'The Raja surrendered on November 20, 1894.' He was exiled and died in Batavia on 20 May 1895.

region.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

ledger.note: November 1894: Lombok passes to the Dutch. 'Lombok and Karangasem became part of the Dutch East Indies, and were administered from Bali'; 'Gusti Gede Jelantik was appointed as Dutch regent in 1894'. The Lombok page dates the annexation of the island to 1895.

region.text: Lombok island, with the Balinese court of Cakranegara and Mataram in the west

ledger.note: 20 November 1894: Balinese rule on Lombok ends with the Raja's surrender.

wars.name: Dutch intervention in Lombok and Karangasem

zones.text: Mataram and Cakranegara in western Lombok, where the Dutch fought in 1894

wars.outcome: Dutch victory in July-November 1894: Mataram palace destroyed by the end of September, Pagesangan palace next, bombardment on 8 November, the Raja's surrender on 20 November; 'Dutch control of Lombok and Karangasem'.
wars.note: A Sasak revolt began in 1891 ('Trouble erupted in 1891'); the Lombok page says the Dutch signed a treaty with Sasak rebels in June 1894, a date not on the intervention page.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundaries on the island; the Balinese held the west and rule over the Sasak east was by overlordship.

sources.title: Lombok

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, as the 'rulers of Lombok (no dossier)' counterpart of the dutch-east-indies 1894 gain and the karangasem-lombok suggestion of the se-02-h and se-03-b reports. Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the page conflict on when the Balinese ruled all of Lombok: the Lombok page says 'by 1750', the intervention page 'from around 1839' (after Mataram's 1838 victory over its rivals); the dossier starts 1750 and records 1838 as a merge; (2) the pages name no Balinese kingdoms on Lombok beyond Cakranegara, Mataram and Pagesangan (the sibling's Pagutan and Kediri are not on them) and give no dates for the four-kingdom split; (3) Karangasem on Bali is placed by a disc; the bali dossier (Cliopatria Bali) draws Karangasem too and records its 1894 loss to the Dutch East Indies, so the Karangasem land is drawn by two dossiers 1849-1894: the vassal tint here is the Lombok overlordship; (4) the date of annexation: 1895 (Lombok page) against the November 1894 surrender (dossier end); (5) the Lombok page's 'treaty with Sasak rebels in June 1894' and the 3 June landing are not reconciled; (6) Makassar's attacks on eastern Lombok (1618) and the VOC's treaty with 'the Sasak Princess of Lombok' are on the Lombok page without dates and belong to earlier dossiers; (7) capital coordinates approximate.
